text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Foreign Minster Dariusz Rosati and Latvia's Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs signed a free trade agreement between the two countries yesterday. Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski and Latvias President Guntis Ulmanis discussed the two countries' integration with the EU and the right to Latvian citizenship of 65,000 Poles in Latvia.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS
- Appreciation of the zloty is unacceptable, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank's deputy president Witold Kozinski said.
Zloty depreciation will proceed at a monthly rate of 1.0 percent, Kozinski said.
- Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) has launched daily flights on the Copenhagen-Szczecin route excluding weekends.
Economy class return tickets are priced at $304 and business class tickets at $725, SAS said.
- Venezuela has contracted two M-28 Skytruck aircrafts for the national guard from the PZL Mielec aircraft maker and is planning to contract another four, PZL Mielec said.
- The Centertel analogue mobile phone operator has signed a roaming agreement with Norway's Telenor telecom allowing Centertel's subscribers to use their phones in Norway as of May 1, Centertel said.
- Germany's Stabernack Jr Partner has invested 12 million marks in a packaging plant construction in Sady, western Poland, since September 1996.
In the next three years Stabernack will invest 28 million marks in a cardboard plant construction and eventually employ 200 workers, the company said.
- The net profit of the Browary Warszawskie (BW) breweries in Warsaw was 15.286 million zlotys last year.
BW's general shareholders meeting paid out 1.35 million zlotys in dividends and the rest went to the company's reserve capital.

- The U.S. World Health Network, which had been mulling the acquisition of the bankrupt Hestja insurance firm before it failed last year, is now planning to buy a stake in the Warta Vita insurance firm, a source who declined to be named said.
- The U.S. Cigna Corporation assurer is planning to buy strategic share stakes in the STU non-life and life insurance firms, Cigna said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Petrochemia Plock, Poland's major refinery, will build a fuel distribution plant and a local pipeline in Ostrow Wielkopolski, central Poland, worth 150 million zlotys.
- The trade unions at the KGHM Polska Miedz copper combine want the state treasury to keep their controlling stake in the combine and pass a 15 percent stake to employees.
- The southern Rzeszow province is planning to spend four million zlotys on constructing and developing three communal waste dumps in the next few years.
- Britain's Know-How Fund will spend two million pounds on training Polish civil service officers for negotiations with the EU institutions.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The U.S. Enron International energy concern will invest $120 million in a power plant construction in Nowa Sarzyna, southeastern Poland, according to a 20 year agreement signed with the Polskie Sieci Energetyczne (PSE) national power grid.
PARKIET
- Bank Wschodno Europejski (BWE) is mulling a listing on the Warsaw bourse.
A bourse listing is one of the possible options to increase share capital but other means are available too, BWE official Jerzy Swiderski said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
